facts.statement: The genus Isanodus was described by Cuny and colleagues in 2006.
The type species of the genus Isanodus is Isanodus paladeji.
Isanodus, meaning "Isan Tooth", is an extinct freshwater shark.
facts.quote: Isanodus ("Isan Tooth") is an extinct freshwater shark

facts.statement: Fossils of Isanodus have been found in the Lower Cretaceous of Phu Phan Thong Locality in Nong Bua Lam Phu, Thailand.
facts.quote: from the Lower Cretaceous of Phu Phan Thong Locality in Nong Bua Lam Phu, Thailand

facts.statement: Two species are currently recognized within the genus Isanodus: I. paladeji and I. nongbualamphuensis.
facts.quote: 2 species are recognised in this genus: I. paladeji and I. nongbualamphuensis

facts.statement: Isanodus is closely related to the genus Heteroptychodus.
facts.quote: They are closely related to Heteroptychodus

facts.statement: The parent group of the genus Isanodus is Lonchidiidae.
Isanodus belongs to the family Lonchidiidae.
Isanodus is classified within the class Chondrichthyes.
Isanodus lived during the Barremian stage, between 125.77 and 121.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Barremian to Barremian (125.77 to 121.4 million years ago)

facts.statement: There are three recorded fossil occurrences of Isanodus in the Paleobiology Database.
